paper.title: Low-Rank Online Dynamic Assortment with Dual Contextual Information

settings.name_in_paper: Low-rank Online Assortment with Dual-contexts (LOAD) problem
unmapped: MNL (multinomial logit) choice feedback: user picks at most one item from the offered assortment; revenue = sum r_i * choice probability
Bilinear utility v_it = p_i^T Phi* q_t with rank-r matrix Phi* in R^{d2 x d1}; user features q_t in R^{d1} i.i.d., fixed item features p_i in R^{d2}
Assortment capacity K (canonical m) out of N items
The learner knows kappa (Assumption 3 lower bound on p(i)p(0)), bounds S_p, S_q, and singular-value/covariance quantities needed to set T_0 and alpha_n
settings.definition_quote: At time $t$, a user with feature vector $q_t \in \bbR^{d_1}$ arrives at the platform. Assume there are $N$ products, each with item feature vector $p_i \in \bbR^{d_2}$ ... The platform offers an assortment $S_t$ of size at most $K$ ... we model the utility $v_{it}$ as a low-rank bilinear form of the dual contexts with $v_{it} = p_i^\top \Phi^* q_t$, where $\Phi^*$ is a rank-$r$ matrix

symbols.T_0: exploration length 4 sigma^2 (C_1 sqrt(d1 d2) + C_2 sqrt(log T))^2 + 2B/(lambda_min(Sigma) m)
symbols.alpha_T: confidence radius (1/kappa)(sigma sqrt(2 df log(1+T/df) + 4 log T) + S_2^2 S_perp sqrt(T m))
symbols.df: (d_1+d_2) r - r^2, dimension of reduced space
symbols.S_2: max(S_p, S_q), bound on item/user feature norms
symbols.S_perp: truncation error bound 288 sigma_1^3/(sigma_r^3 kappa) (3/4 + 8T_0/(kappa B) + 2/(m ||Sigma||)) m r log((d1+d2)/delta)/B S_2^4

conditions: Assumption 1: user features i.i.d., bounded norm S_q, positive definite second moment, whitened features sigma-sub-Gaussian with norm bounded by S_v
Assumption 2: item features bounded by S_p with positive definite Sigma_p
Assumption 3: p_t(i|S,Phi) p_t(0|S,Phi) >= kappa > 0 in a unit Frobenius ball around Phi*
initial estimate satisfies ||Phi_0 - Phi*||_F <= c_2 sqrt(sigma_r)
tuning: T_0 and alpha_n as defined in the theorem, any B > 0
B = b sqrt(T) gives O_tilde(r(d_1+d_2) sqrt(T))

source.label: thm:regretbound
source.quote: Suppose assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop:lowrankest} hold. Define T_0 ..., S_perp ..., alpha_n ... Then applying Algorithm \ref{alg:ELSA-UCB} with $T_0$ and $\alpha_n$, the cumulative regret of our ELSA-UCB policy satisfies ${\calR}_T \le R_{\max} \left( T_0 + 3 + 2 \alpha_T \sqrt{T \cdot 2\cdot df \log(T/df)} + 2S_2^2 S_\perp(T-T_0) \right)$, where $R_{\max} = \max_{i\in [N]} r_i$.

results.notes: Regret defined as expectation of differences of expected revenues -> pseudo_regret, against per-user optimal assortment. Paper's K (capacity) is canonical m. delta inside S_perp is left free in statement. Text says with B = b sqrt(T): R_T = O_tilde(r(d_1+d_2) sqrt(T)) (recorded as r2).

bound.regime: large T, K treated as constant

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 and initial-estimate condition of Proposition 1
tuning: B = b sqrt(T) for a constant b

source.label: thm:regretbound
source.quote: With the choice $B = b\sqrt{T}$ for some constant $b$, we have $S_\perp = O(r/\sqrt{T})$ by definition and therefore the sub-linear regret $\calR_T = \tilde{O}(r(d_1+d_2)\sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Simplification stated in the text after Theorem 1, not a separate formal statement; constants depending on kappa, singular values, K suppressed.

symbols.S_perp: truncation error bound as in Theorem 1

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 and initial-estimate condition of Proposition 1

source.label: cor:regretbound_hp
source.quote: Then by applying Algorithm 2 with $T_0 > 1/\delta$ and $\alpha_n$, the cumulative regret of our ELSA-UCB policy satisfies $\sum_{t=1}^{T} r_t \le R_{\max} \left( T_0 + 2 \alpha_T \sqrt{T \cdot 2\cdot df \log(T/df)} + 2S_2^2 S_\perp(T-T_0) \right)$, with probability at least $1-2\delta$

results.notes: Realized sum of per-round pseudo-regrets r_t bounded with probability >= 1-2 delta.

cited_results.setting_description: d-dimensional contextual MNL dynamic assortment with capacity K
contextual MNL assortment with vectorized outer product of user and item features (dimension d1*d2)
